hotkeys-legend.description:
Escape:			Hide gTile
Enter or Space:	Commit current selection
Left:			Move Left inside Grid
Right:			Move Right inside Grid
Up:				Move Up inside Grid
Down:			Move Down inside Grid
<Shift>Left:		Include column to the Left in selection
<Shift>Right:		Include column to the Right in selection
<Shift>Up:		Include row Above in selection
<Shift>Down:	Include row Below in selection
<Alt>Left:		Move to the monitor on the Left
<Alt>Right:		Move to the monitor on the Right
<Alt>Up:			Move to the monitor Above
<Alt>Down:		Move to the monitor Below
1:				Select the first grid layout
2:				Select the second grid layout
3:				Select the third grid layout
4:				Select the fourth grid layout

With "Show tile labels" enabled, each tile also shows a letter - press two letters to tile the focused window to the rectangle spanning those two tiles.

hotkey-open-settings.tooltip: Open this settings window, landing on the Behavior tab. Clear the binding to disable.

hotkey-cycle-tiling-mode.tooltip: Cycle the Tiling mode setting forward through Off, Rule-based, Traditional (3 windows), Traditional (unlimited), and Scrollable, wrapping around, with an on-screen display showing the new mode. Only affects windows opened afterwards - existing windows stay where they are. Clear the binding to disable.

hotkey-cycle-tiling-mode-backward.tooltip: Same cycle as "Cycle tiling mode", stepping backward - so any mode is at most two presses away in one direction or the other. Clear the binding to disable.

hotkey-focus-column-left.tooltip: Scrollable tiling only: focus the column left of the current one, scrolling it into view. Does nothing in other tiling modes. Clear the binding to disable.

hotkey-focus-column-right.tooltip: Scrollable tiling only: focus the column right of the current one, scrolling it into view. Does nothing in other tiling modes. Clear the binding to disable.

hotkey-move-column-left.tooltip: Scrollable tiling only: swap the focused window's column with its left neighbor. Does nothing in other tiling modes. Clear the binding to disable.

hotkey-move-column-right.tooltip: Scrollable tiling only: swap the focused window's column with its right neighbor. Does nothing in other tiling modes. Clear the binding to disable.

animation.tooltip: Animate the gTile overlay popup (show/hide and grid transitions). Automatic tiling's window animation is controlled separately by "Tiling animation duration" below.

aspect-ratio.tooltip: Whether the popup's grid reflects the current monitor's aspect ratio.

tiling-mode.tooltip:
Off: nothing is tiled automatically. Windows are tiled only when you use the gTile popup, its hotkeys, or the org.gTile.Control D-Bus interface (which is how OhMyDebn's "Tile with gaps" keybindings work).

Rule-based tiling: OhMyDebn's own tile-rules.json matches specific apps to specific spots.

Traditional tiling (3 windows): every new window splits into a binary tree (full screen, then left/right, then upper-right/lower-right, alternating vertical/horizontal), capped at 3 windows - a 4th window discards the tree and starts over at full screen; independent per monitor and workspace; ignores tile-rules.json entirely.

Traditional tiling (unlimited): the same binary-tree splitting but keeps going past 3 windows instead of restarting. Both traditional modes automatically rebalance when a window closes, so the remaining windows reclaim the freed space.

Scrollable tiling (like Niri): every new window opens as its own full-height column to the right of the focused one, at the configured column width, and the screen is a viewport scrolling over the strip of columns - focusing a window scrolls its column into view, and columns scrolled out of view are minimized until focused again (window list, Alt-Tab, the column hotkeys on the Hotkeys tab - Super+comma/period by default - or the org.gTile.Control D-Bus methods FocusColumnLeft/FocusColumnRight and MoveColumnLeft/MoveColumnRight). A lone window fills the whole screen and collapses to a column when a second one opens - and expands again when it's alone. Ignores tile-rules.json entirely.

All automatic modes are independent per monitor and workspace, and a window stays in the layout of the monitor and workspace it opened on - moving it elsewhere by hand doesn't re-tile it there. Cycle through the modes with Super+L / Super+Shift+L (see the Hotkeys tab); switching modes only affects windows opened afterwards.

scrollable-column-width.tooltip: Column width for Scrollable tiling, as a percentage of the usable screen width. At 50% two columns are visible at a time, at 25% four. Widths that don't divide the screen evenly (30%, 40%) leave the remainder empty at the right edge. Only used when Tiling mode is Scrollable tiling. A lone window always fills the whole screen regardless of this setting.

scroll-animation-duration.tooltip: How long windows take to glide and resize into place when automatic tiling rearranges them - Scrollable tiling's scrolling as well as the Traditional modes' splits and rebalances - in milliseconds. 0 disables the animation. Automatically disabled while Cinnamon's system-wide desktop effects are turned off.

maximize-with-gaps.tooltip:
When maximizing a window (titlebar maximize button, Cinnamon's maximize keybinding, or double-clicking the titlebar), leave the existing window-gap margin instead of a true edge-to-edge maximize. Dragging a window to the top edge is not affected - that's a separate top-half tile, not a maximize.

Independent of the Tiling mode setting - applies no matter which mode is selected. Uses the same "Window gaps in pixels" size set above.

Note: Cinnamon no longer considers a gap-maximized window "maximized" internally, so maximizing it again restores it to its original size and position instead of re-maximizing.

useMonitorCenter.tooltip: By default the grid UI shows up in the middle of the active window. With this, it always displays in the middle of the monitor.

showGridOnAllMonitors.description: Show UI on all monitors at the same time

grid1x.tooltip: Each row represents a column. Span is how much space a column should take up compared to the other columns. Default is 1.

grid1y.tooltip: Each row represents a row. Span is how much space a row should take up compared to the other rows. Default is 1.

grid2y.tooltip: Each row represents a row. Span is how much space a row should take up compared to the other rows. Default is 1.
